steps.u: Students hit random 502s on the assignment upload page, maybe 0.3% of requests. Priya Natarajan opened OPS-3317 about it. nginx in front of gunicorn. Can you find the cause?

i.command: ssh web-lb-1.campus.eduportal.internal "grep ' 502 ' /var/log/nginx/access.log | tail -200 | awk '{print \$7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -4"

steps.r:
2026/11/19 14:02:11 [error] 1180#1180: *88213 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.20.4.77, server: portal, request: "POST /api/submissions HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.8.15:8000/api/submissions"
2026/11/19 14:02:40 [error] 1180#1180: *88302 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream ...

steps.a: It isn't upload-specific: every route gets them in proportion to traffic, and the error is 'upstream prematurely closed connection'. That points to connection reuse rather than slow handlers.

steps.r:
1 bind = "0.0.0.0:8000"
2 workers = 8
3 worker_class = "gthread"
4 threads = 4
5 keepalive = 5

i.command: ssh web-lb-1.campus.eduportal.internal "awk '\$9==502 {print \$NF}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | tail -500 | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=\$1} END {print \"p50 upstream_connect_reuse_age=\" a[int(NR/2)]}'"

steps.a: Cause found. nginx keeps idle upstream connections for 75 s, but gunicorn closes idle keep-alive connections after 5 s. When nginx reuses a connection right as gunicorn closes it, the request is sent on a socket the backend is tearing down and nginx returns 502. The failing requests cluster at a reuse age of about 5 s, which matches. The fix is to make the upstream side outlive nginx: set gunicorn keepalive above nginx's keepalive_timeout (e.g. keepalive = 80) or lower nginx keepalive_timeout to below 5 s. POSTs aren't retried by nginx by default, which is why uploads feel it most. I haven't changed the configs, since both hosts are managed by the ops team's Ansible repo.

reference.summary: Diagnosed intermittent 502 errors behind an nginx reverse proxy: the proxy kept idle upstream connections for 75 seconds while gunicorn closed idle keep-alive connections after 5 seconds, so reused connections were sometimes closed mid-request. Failures clustered at a 5-second reuse age; matching the timeouts was recommended but no config was changed.
facts: About 0.3% of requests returned 502 across all routes, not just uploads
nginx logged upstream prematurely closed connection
nginx upstream keepalive_timeout was 75 s and gunicorn keepalive was 5 s
Failing requests clustered at a connection reuse age of about 5 s
The recommended fix (gunicorn keepalive above nginx's timeout) was not applied
